finding: D3 cross-file relation -- adversarial refutation attempt
claim_under_test: response_level_k(wl) * wl  proportional to  F(T=5800, M_k, wl) over 330-850 nm with one shared constant, M = -0.90,-0.50,0.00,+0.50,+0.90
verifier: independent recomputation from the two raw TSVs only; scipy unavailable and unused

input_files.photon_flux_grid.tsv: 18480 rows = 3 T x 35 M x 176 wl

verdict: CORRESPONDENCE ESTABLISHED (not an artefact) -- but it is a property of the REALIGNED data product, and the five levels are not five independent series
verdict_reasons: TRANSFORM IS DISTINGUISHED: with p free (level ~ F * wl**p), the optimum is p = -1.001 and the 1.5x interval is [-1.006, -0.994]; outside it the fit collapses.  level ~ F (p=0) is 198x worse in median deviation (0.2094 vs 0.00106) and 5.6e4x worse in chi2/point; level ~ F*wl (p=+1) is 375x worse in median; level ~ F*wl^2 (p=+2) is 519x worse.

T=5800 UNIQUELY BEST on the rounding-normalised chi2 metric for all five levels: chi2/point = 0.93-1.17 at T=5800 vs 1786-17252 at T=5300 and 2090-17195 at T=6300; no (T,M) pair at any other temperature reaches within 2x of the best median.

M ladder: the claimed M is the argmin of both the median and the chi2 metrics for all five levels; the claimed 5-tuple is RANK 1 of 248832 enumerated tuples, and every one of the 1345 tuples within 2x of it has all five T = 5800.
single shared constant TENABLE: per-level c spreads by 2.0e-4, versus 1.6e-4 expected from rounding alone (chi2 = 3.73 on 4 dof, 5% critical value 9.49).

residual at the claimed solution sits AT the rounding floor (chi2/point ~1.0, and no band point exceeds 1.22x the 3-significant-figure rounding half width), which is the best a 3-significant-figure grid can do.
qualifications: M ASSIGNMENT IS DEGENERATE UNDER THE MEDIAN METRIC the prior workers used: 32 of 248832 5-tuples fall within 1.25x of the best pooled median, and the corridor leaves L1 free over M in [-1.00,-0.45], L2 over [-0.55,-0.20], L3 over [-0.30,+0.20].  In log-ratio terms one M step (median |dlogF| = 3.9e-3) is only ~3x the per-point rounding floor (~1.3e-3), so the MEDIAN metric cannot resolve M at one-ladder-step precision for L1/L2/L3.  T is degenerate only under the median metric too (see below), and the median metric is not a sufficient statistic here.

T=5800 IS UNIQUELY BEST ON THE CHI2/RMS METRIC, but the median metric is misleading: for L1 the best T=5300 median (0.0551) vs best T=5800 (0.0011) is a ratio of ~50, while the chi2 gap is ~1.9e4.  What separates temperatures is that T=5800's residual variance is at the rounding floor (chi2/point 0.93-1.17) while T=5300/6300 are 1.8e3-1.7e4x the floor.

ONLY AFTER WAVELENGTH REALIGNMENT: under raw row indexing (no shift) the pooled median deviation grows from 1.06e-3 to 1.54e-2 (a factor 14.6), and the rms from 1.3e-3 to 0.12. The 330-850 nm band lies entirely in the region where response row i maps to grid row i+1 (median offset 4.84 nm ~ one full 5 nm grid step).  The correspondence is therefore a property of the ALIGNED product, not of the raw tables as published.

THE MEDIAN METRIC'S DEGENERACY IS EXACTLY WHAT THE PRIOR 1.1e-3 FIGURE HIDES: the prior workers reported only that the residual equals the 3-significant-figure rounding floor, which it does (chi2/point ~1).  That number is consistent with BOTH the claimed transform and with a 32-tuple corridor of other (T,M) assignments, and it is a floor imposed by the data storage rather than a property of the underlying physical model.

THE FIVE LEVELS ARE NOT FIVE INDEPENDENT SERIES: the 5x104 band log-matrix is effectively rank 1-2 (participation ratio 1.197, 2nd singular value carries 9.1% of band variance, first carries 90.9%; >= 99.9% of variance needs 2 components).  A 5x104 'match' therefore does not supply 520 independent constraints -- the amplitude ratios alone already fix the M ladder, and a single common shape supplies the rest.

the relation CANNOT BE TESTED below a relative deviation of ~1.3e-3 because photon_flux_cm2 is stored to 3 significant figures; any transform sharing a single constant and landing at that floor is indistinguishable from the claimed one at higher precision with these files.

flux_quantisation.note: flux is stored to 3 significant figures; a match cannot be resolved below a relative deviation of ~1.2e-3 (the 1-sigma rounding floor).  Any transform whose residual sits at that level is UNTESTABLE at higher precision with these files.

shared_constant_test.verdict: single shared constant TENABLE (chi2 below the 5% critical value)

rank2_residual_vs_M_ladder_shape.note: the 2nd component of the level matrix is aligned with the metallicity-ladder difference shape, i.e. the small (1-4%) departures from a single common shape carry the M signature -- which is why the M assignment is still identifiable

3_rank_and_independence.implication: In the band the 5 x 104 log-level matrix is essentially rank 1-2 (participation ratio ~1.2; the 2nd singular value carries <10% of band variance and the first carries >90%).  The five levels are therefore NOT five independent series: they are one common shape plus five amplitudes plus small (1-4%) metallicity-dependent distortions.  A 5x104 'match' is not 520 independent constraints; the amplitude ratios alone already fix the M ladder, and a shared shape suffices for the rest.

explanation.note: the offset is a full grid step in the band, and the local flux slope is steep near the 380-400 nm features, so the raw-index deviation is dominated by a few points

random_pair_reference.note: distribution of the median-rel-dev statistic over ALL 105 (T,M) pairings x 5 levels, claimed transform.  Used as the 'no assignment at all' reference.

5_shuffled_null.note: destroys wavelength correspondence while preserving each level's own shape; an arbitrarily reshuffled response still leaves a much larger residual, so the claimed 0.1% residual is not obtainable from a random association
